svg.title: Language disorders are overlapping clinical profiles
svg.desc: A profile matrix for five aphasia patterns, three cards distinguishing pure word deafness, pure alexia, and apraxia of speech, and schematic broad lesion distributions and disconnections.
svg.text: Language disorders are overlapping clinical profiles
Task patterns help separate aphasia, modality-specific access disorders, and motor-speech impairment.
Typical tendencies—not diagnostic rules. Lesion boundaries, disconnections, recovery, and co-occurring sensory or motor disorders vary across patients.
Relative sparing does not mean normal.
Naming difficulty also occurs in most other aphasias.
Symbols summarize the overall profile, not a diagnostic score.
B. Selective dissociations and a motor-speech bottleneck

text.tspan: Spoken words may arrive as unintelligible
speech can be much better preserved.
Reading is severely impaired, often slow
and letter by letter. Spoken language and
and oral reading may all look poor because

svg.text: The same test failure can arise at different stages; interpretation depends on the full profile and the lesion—not a single cell in a table.
